{
 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Tutorial: accelerating ultranest with simulation-based inference (SBI)\n",
    "\n",
    "In this tutorial you will learn:\n",
    "\n",
    " - How to specify a mock data generator in addition to the likelihood\n",
    " - How to train a simulation-based inference model to predict a posterior distribution (neural posterior estimation)\n",
    " - How to verify that the simulation-based inference trained well\n",
    " - How to use SBI-NPE to accelerate the UltraNest nested sampling run\n",
    "\n",
    "In this example, we fit a Voigt line in a spectrum."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import corner\n",
    "import ultranest\n",
    "import ultranest.simbase.minisbi\n",
    "\n",
    "rng = np.random.default_rng(123)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Defining the model"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Gaussian measurement noise"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "First, we need our physical model function of the intrinsic spectrum, and also predict the noise level. We assume a Voigt line shape and constant noise."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "noise_std = 0.1"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "N_DATA = 1000\n",
    "x = np.geomspace(0.55, 0.75, N_DATA)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "parameter_names = [\"amplitude\", \"center_x\", \"width\", \"background\", \"slope\"]\n",
    "N_PARAMS = len(parameter_names)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Define the model spectrum function, given model parameters"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from scipy.special import voigt_profile"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "sigma_instrumental = 0.001 # nominal resolution of the spectrograph"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 41,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "The history saving thread hit an unexpected error (OperationalError('attempt to write a readonly database')).History will not be written to the database.\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "def generate_mean_and_noise(theta, idx=0, seed=0):\n",
    "    amplitude, center_x, width, background, slope = theta\n",
    "    signal = amplitude * voigt_profile(x - center_x, sigma_instrumental, width) + background + (x / center_x) ** slope\n",
    "\n",
    "    return {\n",
    "        'mean':      signal,\n",
    "        'noise_std': signal * 0 + noise_std,  # same noise for each data point\n",
    "    }"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The received idx and seed are not used here. They are integers, in case randomness in the physics model is needed."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Our true parameters for this example:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "theta_true = [0.0042, 0.656279, 0.001, 0.2, -1.]"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "plt.errorbar(\n",
    "    x=x,\n",
    "    y=generate_mean_and_noise(theta_true)['mean'],\n",
    "    capsize=0,\n",
    ")\n",
    "plt.fill_between(\n",
    "    x,\n",
    "    generate_mean_and_noise(theta_true)['mean'] - generate_mean_and_noise(theta_true)['noise_std'],\n",
    "    generate_mean_and_noise(theta_true)['mean'] + generate_mean_and_noise(theta_true)['noise_std'],\n",
    "    alpha=0.1,\n",
    ")\n",
    "plt.yscale('log');"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "A beautiful spectrum of a line, on top of a slightly sloped continuum."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Prior distribution"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Define our prior distribution as usual, based on unit cube transforms."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 10,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def prior_transform(u):\n",
    "    result = u.copy()\n",
    "    # amplitude (index 0): log-uniform [1e-2, 1e2]\n",
    "    result[0] = 10**(-4 + u[0] * 4)\n",
    "    # center_x (index 1): uniform [0.65, 0.66]\n",
    "    result[1] = 0.65 + u[1] * 0.01\n",
    "    # width (index 2): uniform [1e-4, 0.01]\n",
    "    result[2] = 10**(-4 + 2 * u[2])\n",
    "    # background level (index 3): uniform [-1, 1]\n",
    "    result[3] = -1 + 2 * u[3]\n",
    "    # slope (index 4): uniform [-2, +2]\n",
    "    result[4] = -2 + 4 * u[4]\n",
    "    return result\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Generate noisy data"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### The observed data we will fit"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Going from the model above to data is trivial, with a Gaussian random number generator:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def inject_noise(mean_props, rng):\n",
    "    return rng.normal(mean_props['mean'], mean_props['noise_std'])"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 12,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "obs_spectrum = inject_noise(generate_mean_and_noise(theta_true), rng)\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.plot(x, obs_spectrum)\n",
    "plt.yscale('log')"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Generate mock data - Prior predictive checks"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Here are some example data sets when we sampled from the prior. These show the diversity of data we consider reasonable a priori:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 13,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "for i in range(10):\n",
    "    u = rng.uniform(size=N_PARAMS)\n",
    "    params = prior_transform(u)\n",
    "    plt.plot(x, inject_noise(generate_mean_and_noise(params), rng))\n",
    "    plt.yscale('log')\n",
    "    plt.ylim(1e-2, 40)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Data likelihood"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "We adopt a corresponding Gaussian likelihood function, that we will use at the end with ultranest to improve upon the SBI approach."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 14,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def loglikelihood(mean_props, noisy_data):\n",
    "    # the usual Gaussian likelihood function, comparing data to the model, under noise\n",
    "    return np.sum(\n",
    "        -0.5 * np.log(2.0 * np.pi)\n",
    "        - np.log(mean_props['noise_std'])\n",
    "        - 0.5 * ((noisy_data - mean_props['mean']) / mean_props['noise_std']) ** 2\n",
    "    )"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Simulation-based inference"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The simulation-based inference trains a neural network to predict a simple factorized posterior distribution on the unit hypercube. \n",
    "\n",
    "The training pipeline is highly efficient, reusing generated model with different noise."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Sampled datasets will be cached internally to a folder."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 15,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "folder = 'mygaussline'"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 16,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# optional: clear cache whenever you change the prior or model function\n",
    "!rm -rf mygaussline/"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "This happens efficiently in batches (using joblib.Memory). Some helper functions that call our functions in a loop:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 17,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from ultranest.simbase.minisbi.utils import make_memory, make_cached_generate"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 18,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "memory = make_memory(folder)\n",
    "generate_noiseless_batch = make_cached_generate(\n",
    "    memory, prior_transform, generate_mean_and_noise\n",
    ")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Training the model"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Next train a simple neural network to predict a posterior distribution."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 19,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from ultranest.simbase.minisbi.npe import train_npe"
   ]
  },

   "execution_count": 20,

      "  Epoch  68/390  train_loss=-8.4102  val_loss=-8.3823  fresh_simulator_evals=17408  [1/10]\n",
      "  Epoch  69/390  train_loss=-8.4946  val_loss=-8.5039  fresh_simulator_evals=17664  [2/10]\n",
      "  Epoch  70/390  train_loss=-8.4990  val_loss=-8.3605  fresh_simulator_evals=17920  [3/10]\n",
      "  Epoch  71/390  train_loss=-8.5852  val_loss=-8.5295  fresh_simulator_evals=18176  *\n",

      "  Epoch  75/390  train_loss=-8.7245  val_loss=-8.9182  fresh_simulator_evals=19200  *\n",
      "  Epoch  76/390  train_loss=-8.7031  val_loss=-8.7492  fresh_simulator_evals=19456  [1/10]\n",
      "  Epoch  77/390  train_loss=-8.7990  val_loss=-8.6333  fresh_simulator_evals=19712  [2/10]\n",
      "  Epoch  78/390  train_loss=-8.6591  val_loss=-8.7141  fresh_simulator_evals=19968  [3/10]\n",

   "source": [
    "model = train_npe(\n",
    "    # our folder\n",
    "    folder=folder,\n",
    "    # our (costly) model function\n",
    "    generate_noiseless_batch=generate_noiseless_batch,\n",
    "    # our cheap noisy generator:\n",
    "    inject_noise=inject_noise,\n",
    "    # our model parameters\n",
    "    n_params=N_PARAMS,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Parameters related to training strategy:\n",
    "\n",
    "    # seed for randomness\n",
    "    base_seed=12345,\n",
    "    # how long to train: Choose how long you want to wait - the higher the better.\n",
    "    max_model_evals=100000,\n",
    "    # optional: if > 1, evaluate models in parallel (with joblib.Parallel)\n",
    "    num_processes=1,\n",
    "    # the full history of noise-free models generated with generate_mean_and_noise is kept.\n",
    "    # they are reused and additional datasets are generated with fresh noise\n",
    "    # fresh_example_fraction sets the balance between freshly generated models and reuse of previously generated models\n",
    "    # if the model is cheap, can be 1.0. \n",
    "    # Probably should not be much lower than 0.001. -- if the loss becomes extremely small (-300), the network memorized all samples.\n",
    "    fresh_example_fraction=0.01,\n",
    "    # choose how many new samples are generated in each epoch\n",
    "    # this sets the number of model evaluations per epoch\n",
    "    # Note: This sets the batch size seen by the network in each evaluation, by batch_size=fresh_sim_batch_size / fresh_example_fraction - you probably want batch_size of O(1000)\n",
    "    fresh_sim_batch_size=32,\n",
    "    # neural network training is somewhat stochastic and may not give an improvement in each epoch\n",
    "    # set the patience to how many epochs to wait for a significant improvement\n",
    "    # in any case, the best neural network is kept.\n",
    "    patience=10,\n",
    "    # what loss improvement is designated a substantial improvement\n",
    "    patience_min_delta=0.01,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # parameters for the neural network architecture and learning\n",
    "\n",
    "    # learning rate - need to chose this depending on the batch size. \n",
    "    # Increase if loss is changing slowly, decrease if the loss becomes erratic. \n",
    "    # Try 1e-3, 1e-4, etc.\n",
    "    npe_lr=3e-4,\n",
    "    # maximum width of the layers, 1024 is a decent default, but worth trying other values\n",
    "    npe_width=512,\n",
    "    # maximum number of layers. 'cascade' is not very sensitive to this parameter.\n",
    "    npe_depth=6,\n",
    "    # shape: \n",
    "    # - 'rectangular' - a classic MLP where each of the npe_depth layer has npe_width neurons\n",
    "    # - 'triangular' - a funnel-shaped MLP, with each next layer decreasing linearly in width\n",
    "    # - 'cascade' - subsequent layers are half the width, half the neurons are forwarded to the next layer, the other half skip to the final layer.\n",
    "    # 'cascade' is recommended, because it avoids having to play much with npe_width and npe_depth - it contains both a wide and a deep network.\n",
    "    # the neural network layers can be of equal layer width\n",
    "    layer_shape='cascade',\n",
    "    # activation function\n",
    "    npe_activation_cls='ReLU',\n",
    ")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The meaning of the training output is as follows:\n",
    "\n",
    "The **loss** is the log-density of the predicted posterior distribution at the true parameter values.\n",
    "\n",
    "The **training loss** is what the optimizer sees. Ideally, this should not stall.\n",
    "\n",
    "The **validation loss** is the posterior density of independent samples generated at the beginning and kept separate. These mock data and their true parameters are not seen by the training and kept fixed. The validation loss should keep improving (decreasing).\n",
    "\n",
    "The **fresh_simulator_evals** gives the number of model calls performed so far.\n",
    "\n",
    "The last column gives a star when the model is improving, and otherwise counting up until *patience* epochs give no improvements.\n",
    "\n",
    "At the end, the best model is kept."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

    "### Checking the SBI model: rank histogram"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "First, we check that the model gives reliable posteriors, with a rank histogram.\n",
    "\n",
    "We generate from the prior, and sample posterior samples. Ideally, the rank of the prior samples and the rank of the posterior samples are on a line (see [Simulation-based calibration paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.06788))."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 28,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from ultranest.simbase.minisbi.plot import rank_histogram"

      "  return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(x, -500.0, 500.0)))\n",
      "Rank histogram: 100%|█████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████| 5000/5000 [00:00<00:00, 8801.27sim/s]\n"

   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Next, we check whether the x% credible intervals contain the true value in x% of cases:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 31,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from ultranest.simbase.minisbi.plot import parameter_coverage_test"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 32,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stderr",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [

    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "coverage, fig, axes = parameter_coverage_test(\n",
    "    model=model,\n",
    "    generate_noiseless_batch=generate_noiseless_batch,\n",
    "    inject_noise=inject_noise,\n",
    "    prior_transform=prior_transform,\n",
    "    n_params=N_PARAMS,\n",
    "    folder=folder,\n",
    "    n_test=500,\n",
    "    credible_levels=np.linspace(0.05, 0.99, 20).tolist(),\n",

   "cell_type": "markdown",

   "source": [
    "These should follow the diagonal (red dashed).\n",
    "\n",
    "Most of them look good. The amplitude parameter is slightly off, but not too wild.\n",
    "\n",
    "If not, the posterior for that parameter is not well-calibrated (too narrow or too wide error bars). You might be able to improve this by choosing a larger neural network."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 33,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {

     ]

   "source": [
    "print(\"  Empirical coverage at nominal 90% level:\")\n",
    "levels = np.linspace(0.05, 0.99, 20)\n",
    "idx_90 = np.argmin(np.abs(levels - 0.90))\n",
    "for i, name in enumerate(parameter_names):\n",
    "    print(f\"    {name:12s}: {coverage[idx_90, i]:.3f}  (nominal=0.900)\")\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### ultranest-sbi: SBI-accelerated nested sampling"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Setting up the accelerated inference"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Here we run nested sampling using the NPE posterior as a reparameterisation.\n",
    "\n",
    "This allows nested sampling to start at a shrunk-down prior. To ensure identical inference as if we had started with the full prior, we need to correct the likelihood function by a penalty.\n",
    "\n",
    "* The nested sampler samples t ~ Uniform(0,1)^d.\n",
    "* The prior transform maps:   t -> u -> theta\n",
    "* The log-likelihood includes a correction: loglike(theta) - log q(u | x_obs)\n",
    "\n",
    "The correction ensures that the evidence integral and posterior samples\n",
    "are correct with respect to the original flat prior over u (and thus\n",
    "the physical prior over theta)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 34,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# a helper object defining the distribution, its transform and log-posterior\n",
    "klp_transform = KLPTransform(**distribution_parameters)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 35,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "class _State:\n",
    "    last_t = None\n",
    "state = _State()\n",
    "\n",
    "# warp the prior by the NPE distribution\n",
    "def warped_prior_transform(t):\n",
    "    # keep the last state for likelihood\n",
    "    state.last_t = t.copy()\n",
    "    # [0,1]^d -> [0,1]^d with the SBI posterior warp\n",
    "    u     = klp_transform.transform(t).astype(float)\n",
    "    # [0,1]^d -> physical parameters\n",
    "    theta = prior_transform(u)\n",
    "    return theta\n",
    "\n",
    "# correct the likelihood for the warp\n",
    "def corrected_log_likelihood(theta):\n",
    "    mp   = generate_mean_and_noise(theta=theta, idx=0, seed=0)\n",
    "    # compute our model likelihood\n",
    "    logL = loglikelihood(mp, obs_spectrum)\n",
    "    # compute neural posterior density\n",
    "    log_jac = klp_transform.log_jacobian(state.last_t)\n",
    "    return logL + log_jac\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Setting up the accelerated sampler"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Build our accelerated ultranest-sbi sampler:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 36,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "sampler = ultranest.ReactiveNestedSampler(\n",
    "    parameter_names,\n",
    "    corrected_log_likelihood,\n",
    "    warped_prior_transform,\n",
    "    log_dir=folder,\n",
    "    resume='overwrite',\n",
    ")"
   ]
  },
  {

   "metadata": {},

   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

   ]

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Notice that the ultranest-sbi posterior (orange) is much narrower than the SBI posterior (blue), because SBI lost a lot of information. Nevertheless, the blue distribution provides a useful starting point for nested sampling."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Takeaways"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "* In addition to the usual model and its likelihood, we defined a data simulator that can generate data.\n",
    "\n",
    "* We have learned to train a simulation-based inference (SBI) neural posterior estimator (NPE) model for obtaining a fast posterior distribution.\n",
    "\n",
    "* We checked that SBI posterior is amortized to behave well across the entire prior.\n",
    "\n",
    "* We used the SBI posterior on our data to get a starting point for a posterior distribution. This distribution has lost some information.\n",
    "\n",
    "* We used ultranest on top of the SBI posterior to get the posterior samples from the true posterior.\n",
    "\n",
    "* This ultranest-sbi approach effectively \"skips\" many initial nested sampling iterations, zooming into a data-driven guess for the posterior location. Because the SBI posterior is virtually always too wide, nested sampling is then fast to integrate to the actual posterior bulk.\n",
    "\n",
    "**Limitations**: The posterior distribution used by the neural network is factorized and not optimal for challenging distributions. With a different, more sophisticated sbi package, better neural posteriors could be learned, but that would mean more complexity as well.\n",
    "\n",
    "When using this in publications, please refer to it as **ultranest-sbi**, to distinguish it from ultranest."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "#### Further reading\n",

    "* https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1912789117 \"The frontier of simulation-based inference\", Cranmer, Brehmer, Louppe, 2020"
   ]
